key_insight: UltraQuant shows that 4-bit KV-cache compression can improve both cache residency and serving latency for long-context, multi-round agents without sacrificing the system-level goals that matter in deployment.
engineering_relevance: The work is directly relevant to LLM serving engineers because it targets the KV cache bottleneck under real concurrency pressure and demonstrates an AMD GPU path with optimized decode attention and FP4-style execution.
method: Uses 4-bit KV caching with TurboQuant-style rotation and codebook quantization as a quality anchor
Adds practical robustness choices: asymmetric K/V treatment, Walsh-Hadamard rotation, QJL removal, and block-scale variants
Implements an AMD-focused serving path with optimized kernels and UltraQuant using FP8 queries, FP4 KV tensors, UE8M0 group scales, and native scaled-MFMA
evidence_signal: On a long-context, multi-turn agentic workload, UltraQuant improved P50 time-to-first-token by 3.47x in late cache-pressured rounds and by 2.3x overall, while increasing output throughput by 1.63x versus the FP8 KV baseline.
watch_item: The gains depend on specialized AMD CDNA4 support and optimized kernels, so portability and kernel maturity may be a practical deployment constraint.
paper_title: UltraQuant: 4-bit KV Caching for Context-Heavy Agents
